\begin{frame}{Harmonic Motion}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item A mass $m$ on a spring of stiffness $k$ oscillates.
    \item The angular frequency is $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$.
    \item The period is $T = 2\pi/\omega$.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{The Equation of Motion}
  Newton's second law for the spring gives
  \begin{equation*}
    m \ddot{x} = -k x .
  \end{equation*}
  Its solution is
  \begin{equation*}
    x(t) = A \cos(\omega t + \phi).
  \end{equation*}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Energy}
  The two forms of energy are
  \begin{align*}
    K &= \tfrac{1}{2} m v^2, \\
    U &= \tfrac{1}{2} k x^2,
  \end{align*}
  and their sum $E = K + U$ stays constant.
\end{frame}
